data.name: Shankar
data.short_meaning: God of auspiciousness, peace and prosperity
data.long_meaning: Shankar is a Sanskrit name which means 'The Benevolent One', 'The God of Auspiciousness', 'The God of Peace and Prosperity'. This name is derived from the Hindu god Shiva, who is the god of destruction and regeneration. Shankar is a powerful name that signifies strength, courage, wisdom and peace. It is believed that those named Shankar possess the qualities of Shiva and are blessed with his divine protection and grace.
data.spiritual_meaning: Shankar is a spiritual name that represents the divine qualities of the Hindu god Shiva. It signifies the power of destruction and regeneration, and the ultimate goal of spiritual growth and self-realization.
data.numerology_meaning: Shankar is a name that vibrates with the energy number 1. This number represents leadership, independence and initiative. Those named Shankar are natural born leaders who are self-motivated and have the ability to inspire others. They are also independent thinkers and are not afraid to take risks.

data.cultural_impact: The name Shankar holds significant cultural impact in India, as it is derived from one of the most revered and worshipped gods in Hinduism. Shiva is known as the god of destruction and transformation, and his name Shankar represents his benevolent and peaceful aspects. The name Shankar has been passed down through generations in Hindu families and is often given to boys as a name that represents strength, courage, and auspiciousness.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Shankar holds deep significance as it is a reflection of the divine qualities of the Hindu god Shiva. Shankar signifies the eternal cycle of destruction and rebirth, representing the idea that everything in life is impermanent and that even in destruction, there is the potential for new growth and renewal. The name is believed to bring blessings of peace, prosperity, and protection from the divine power of Shiva. Those named Shankar are said to embody the qualities of wisdom, courage, and spiritual strength, and are believed to be connected to the divine source of all creation. Ultimately, Shankar is a name that inspires a deeper connection to the divine and the eternal cycle of life, death, and rebirth.

historical_references.reference: Shankara was a prominent philosopher, theologian and reformer of the Advaita (non-dualistic) school of Hindu philosophy in the 8th century AD. He is often referred to as 'Adi Shankaracharya' or the 'First Shankara', as he is considered the founder of the Advaita monastic order and the author of various influential texts including commentaries on the Upanishads and the Bhagavad Gita.

Shankara, also known as Shankaracharya, was a renowned Hindu philosopher, theologian and reformer in the 13th century AD who played a significant role in the Bhakti movement. He composed many hymns and poems, popularly known as the Shankara Devotional Poems, which continue to be widely recited in temples and shrines across India.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Shankar holds significant religious and philosophical meaning for Hindus, representing the deity Shiva, the god of destruction and transformation. In modern times, the name Shankar has gained popularity beyond religious contexts and is often associated with trends related to spirituality, yoga, and meditation. Social media platforms such as Instagram, Twitter, and LinkedIn are popular spaces where individuals with the name Shankar share their personal practices, inspirational quotes, and insights related to these trends.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted individual named Radha Shankar in Bali, Indonesia attributes much of their spiritual journey to their name Shankar, which means "God of auspiciousness, peace and prosperity". They believe their name has guided them on the path of righteousness.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Shankar symbolizes the embodiment of supreme consciousness and destructive force in the universe. As Shiva, Shankar represents the the transformative power that destroys ignorance and bestows enlightenment. He is the ultimate reality and the cosmic dancer.
